title: Add OctoPrint browser integration smoke test
description: Add a standalone browser integration smoke test for the packaged plugin. The shell driver should use uv to create a fresh temporary Python 3.11+ environment, install the latest compatible OctoPrint, the pinned playwright-testing dependency group, and the freshly built plugin wheel. Launch OctoPrint itself on localhost with a fixed repo-local basedir and no interactive authentication; use a disposable local admin with automatic localhost login so the real admin settings UI is available. By default, wipe the basedir before each run; support --preserve-basedir for deliberate stateful/debug runs. Use Playwright-managed Firefox, installed into the temporary runtime. Run headless by default and support --headed and --verbose. Keep this separate from run-tests.sh. The test is settings-only for now; no virtual printer or physical hardware is required.
design: Use a shell driver plus a Python Playwright test. Build the wheel on every run so the test exercises current package contents and asset metadata. Use a fixed basedir under .tmp for inspectable server state, with a separate .tmp/octoprint-smoke-artifacts/ directory for screenshots, Playwright traces, and logs. Start the server on an automatically selected localhost port, poll for readiness, terminate it on exit, and retain the basedir/artifacts for diagnosis. Write the complete OctoPrint log to an artifact file and stream it with --verbose; print a useful tail on failure. Use a fresh temporary uv environment per run while relying on uv caching for speed. Install the latest OctoPrint, keep Playwright pinned in a dedicated playwright-testing dependency group, and install the matching Playwright Firefox build in the temporary runtime. Seed a disposable admin account and configure localhost autologin to avoid an interactive login while preserving access to the admin settings UI.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Standalone shell driver creates a fresh uv-managed Python 3.11+ environment and installs the latest compatible OctoPrint, pinned playwright-testing dependencies, and the freshly built local plugin wheel.
- [x] Driver installs the Playwright-managed Firefox build into the temporary runtime.
- [x] Driver launches OctoPrint on localhost with a fixed inspectable basedir, no interactive login, and automatic localhost admin login.
- [x] Driver wipes the basedir by default and supports --preserve-basedir for opt-in stateful runs.
- [x] Driver supports headless/headed operation and gives actionable failure output when Playwright Firefox cannot be installed or launched.
- [x] Playwright test opens the real Repeating Command settings page and verifies plugin asset loading and viewmodel initialization.
- [x] Test fails on JavaScript page errors, console errors, failed plugin asset requests, or failed settings API requests; ordinary console warnings are allowed.
- [x] Test exercises three rules: add, reorder, remove, edit every rule field, save, reload, and verify final order and values.
- [x] Test writes full server logs and captures a screenshot plus Playwright trace on failure under .tmp/octoprint-smoke-artifacts/.
- [x] Driver cleans up the temporary environment and server process, while preserving the basedir and failure artifacts.
- [x] README documents the standalone command and prerequisites; run-tests.sh remains unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the Playwright browser smoke test

title: Avoid transient fallback execution during print state transitions
description: Observed on rpi5 last print 2026-11-13, PS Rod_Hole_Fit_Coupon.gcode. PrintStarted at 14:59:43 starts unfiltered 10s_exhaust_fan.sh immediately; PRINTING state arrives ~0.1s later and switches to filtered fan_on.sh. Already-running fallback still sends OFF at 14:59:56, potentially overriding active filtered fan rule. FINISHING at 16:40:22 starts fallback again before PrintDone cancels timer; script still sends OFF at 16:40:34. Need regression tests for actual run_first execution and in-flight commands, and transition handling that avoids unintended fallback commands. All 567 subprocesses returned 0; output showed two OFF commands. Both rules configured repeating, filtered rule matches PRINTING OR cooling.
close_reason: Resolve PRINTING filters at PrintStarted, suppress fallback during FINISHING/CANCELLING, handle PrintCancelled, and invalidate replaced timer callbacks. Added immediate-execution and in-flight callback regressions. All 28 Python tests and 6 frontend cases pass; isolated rpi5 real-timer harness passed 10 lifecycles with saved settings and mocked commands.

title: Redesign RepeatingCommand v2 around devices, modes, and ordered rules
description:
Evolve the existing RepeatingCommand plugin into v2 using devices, modes, and ordered rules. Keep the plugin identity and installation/update path. Preserve generic command scheduling alongside device automation.

Problem
Rules currently combine conditions, shell commands, and repetition. Timed shell scripts retain delayed actions after a rule changes: a sleeping pulse script can send OFF after a continuous-ON rule takes over. Timer cancellation does not cancel an executing script. Active behavior and its cause are also difficult to inspect.

Proposed model
- Devices define named commands (for example ON/OFF) and a default mode.
- Modes define behavior: set state, pulse with independent on/off durations, repeat a command, and run once on activation. The plugin owns scheduling; pulse scripts do not sleep.
- Ordered rules choose a device's desired mode; first matching rule wins per device, with an explicit default when none match.
- Conditions support explicit ALL/ANY groups over printer lifecycle/state and M117 text. Avoid implicit OR semantics.
- Reconcile events against the desired mode. An unchanged mode does not restart timers or repeat entry actions. Transitions invalidate pending actions before applying the next mode.
- Serialize execution per device and guard against stale callbacks and delayed command completions. Define how command failures and hung commands affect transitions; cancellation of a timer alone is insufficient.
- Show the current mode, matching rule/reason, next scheduled transition, and command errors in the UI.

Reference fan configuration
Device: exhaust fan, ON=fan_on.sh, OFF=fan_off.sh, default OFF.
Priority order:
1. Completed/cancelled/failed session selects OFF.
2. M117 contains warming OR cooling selects continuous ON during the applicable print session.
3. Active print selects pulse: ON 10 seconds, OFF 50 seconds.
4. Default OFF.
Completion must override lingering M117 text; a new print must clear terminal-session precedence. Print Complete text should allow prompt OFF before PrintDone arrives. Define session lifetime so stale M117 text cannot reactivate a finished fan.

Lifecycle and reliability
Specify behavior for pause/resume, finishing, cancellation, failure, disconnect, disable, settings edits, plugin shutdown, and restart. For the fan, completion/cancellation/failure/disconnect/disable should select OFF. Make lifecycle/default behavior configurable where appropriate for other devices. Do not promise cleanup after process crash or power loss; an external controller lease/watchdog is a possible future capability.

Compatibility and migration
Version the settings schema and migrate legacy repeat/run-once rules with their ordering, intervals, filtering semantics, and activation behavior intact. Preserve existing behavior rather than inferring device semantics from arbitrary scripts. Users intentionally opt into converting timed scripts to plugin-owned pulse modes. Provide a reviewable migration summary and recovery path. Keep package/plugin identity; target a v2 release.

Acceptance criteria
- The reference fan setup pulses during ordinary printing, holds ON during warming/cooling, and turns OFF at completion or the defined terminal lifecycle events.
- Switching from pulse to continuous cannot leave a scheduled or in-flight pulse OFF able to determine the final fan state.
- Repeated equivalent events do not restart a mode; devices execute independently with serialized commands within each device.
- Generic repeat and run-once scheduling remain supported and legacy migration has representative compatibility coverage.
- Deterministic scheduler tests cover timing boundaries, simultaneous lifecycle/M117 events, stale callbacks, command failures, and restart/settings transitions.
- The settings UI can configure devices, modes, explicit conditions, and priority; runtime status explains the selected behavior.
- Documentation explains execution timing, lifecycle policy, migration, and crash limitations.

Implementation areas / follow-up breakdown
1. Finalize settings schema and lifecycle/session semantics, including command timeout and failure policy.
2. Implement per-device reconciliation, serialized execution, and cancellable scheduler with deterministic tests.
3. Implement modes and condition/rule evaluation.
4. Implement legacy migration and compatibility tests.
5. Build configuration UI and runtime diagnostics.
6. Document and validate the fan configuration; prepare v2 release.

Open design decisions
Exact UI terminology; how modes reference commands; pause and restart defaults; command timeout/process supervision; and which lifecycle policies are configurable. Resolve these before implementation, without expanding the initial scope into a general workflow graph.

title: Avoid blocking OctoPrint hooks for run-once commands
description: Merge review found run-once executes run_command synchronously from _refresh_timer, including the M117 queuing hook. A long script can block queuing or the event thread. Dispatch run-once commands in a background worker, keep duplicate activation protection, and add a regression that verifies hook return while a command is still running.
close_reason: Dispatch run-once scripts on daemon workers, protect activation bookkeeping with a lock, and share command logging. Regressions verify both M117 and printer-state hooks return while a script is still running and duplicate events do not launch another worker.

close_reason: Diagnosed native build probe linker error: Xcode 26 clang was linking against the newer Command Line Tools macOS 27.2 SDK (unknown architecture arm64e.x1).
